name: State v. Walker
note: For aggravated murder under division (A), purpose and prior calculation and design are separate. The court held the evidence did not support the planning element, while leaving the felony-murder conviction in place.

name: Cincinnati v. Ilg
note: A defendant may challenge the specific test result or the operation of the machine used in the case. That distinction matters even though the general reliability of an approved device cannot be attacked in the same way.

name: State v. Polizzi
note: The court held that proportionality review does not require considering the total number of consecutive sentences or the aggregate prison term. Read this opinion alongside the statutory findings and the appellate review standard.

name: State v. Gwynne
note: On reconsideration, the court vacated its 2022 decision. The plurality explained the clear-and-convincing standard under R.C. 2953.08(G)(2) and upheld the consecutive sentences. Also read the later Polizzi decision.

name: Bruns v. Green
note: When terminating a shared-parenting plan and designating the residential and custodial parent, the court held that the child’s best interest controls. Distinguish termination from modifying a decree under a different statutory division.

name: State v. Bethel
issue: Successive postconviction petitions and suppressed evidence
note: A defendant asserting a Brady claim in an untimely or successive postconviction petition can show unavoidable prevention by establishing that the prosecution suppressed the evidence. This does not dispose of the separate statutory requirements or the merits.

name: State v. Ruff
note: Merger turns on the defendant’s conduct, the import of the offenses, and animus. Separate convictions can stand for offenses of dissimilar import, offenses committed separately, or offenses committed with separate animus.

name: State v. Bollar
note: The court held that the mandatory multiple-specification rule can require separate prison terms for qualifying firearm specifications even when the underlying felony offenses merge.
